prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1399; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and said they had been sitting in the driver's seat when the impact occurred. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and gave a clear account of how the crash happened.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos and the vehicle damage, which line up with the impact described. The other driver and two independent witnesses also confirm the collision happened as the claimant described it.

Entry 3: Claimant reports a shoulder injury from the impact and has provided initial treatment records. It is not yet clear whether this injury came from the crash, so medical review is pending. No earlier injury to the same area is known.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that nothing suggests the vehicle damage predates the start of coverage. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation. Seating position in the vehicle is still not fully clear from the records, so this will be clarified at the next interview.

Entry 6: Treatment has increased to many times the usual amount for this type of shoulder injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added several weeks after the crash. Medical bill review and an independent records check are now scheduled before any decision on the injury portion of the claim.
